statement: The function returns a result r (an i64) and r is the minimum total number of increments needed to make nums strictly increasing. Formally, r is the least integer for which there exists an integer array b of length n such that: (a) for every i with 0 <= i < n, b[i] >= nums[i]; (b) for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, b[i] < b[i+1]; and (c) sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (b[i] - nums[i]) = r. Equivalently, every strictly increasing integer array c of length n with c[i] >= nums[i] for all i has sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(c[i]-nums[i]) >= r, and some such c attains equality.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, min_operations(nums) returns a result; it does not fail, panic, access out of bounds, or overflow in i64 arithmetic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r <= 10000*n + n*(n-1)/2 - sum_{i=0}^{n-1} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, nums[i] < nums[i+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r = max(0, nums[0] + 1 - nums[1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n = 2 and for every i with 0 <= i < 2, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r = n*(n-1)/2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000, and there exists an integer c such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, r = n*(n-1).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000, and there exists an integer c such that nums[i] = c - i for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let nums' be the array of length n with nums'[i] = nums[i] + d for every i. If min_operations(nums) returns r and min_operations(nums') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000; and let d be an integer such that for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] + d <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, there exists an integer array b of length n such that for every i with 0 <= i < n, b[i] >= nums[i]; for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, b[i] < b[i+1]; and sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(b[i]-nums[i]) = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, for every integer array c of length n such that c[i] >= nums[i] for all 0 <= i < n and c[i] < c[i+1] for all 0 <= i < n-1, we have sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(c[i]-nums[i]) >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns r, for every l and u with 0 <= l <= u < n, r is greater than or equal to the least integer k for which there exists an integer array c of length u-l+1 such that c[j] >= nums[l+j] for all 0 <= j <= u-l, c[j] < c[j+1] for all 0 <= j < u-l, and sum_{j=0}^{u-l}(c[j]-nums[l+j]) = k.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, r >= max(0, nums[i] + 1 - nums[i+1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, there exists an integer array b of length n such that b[i] >= nums[i] for all 0 <= i < n, b[i] < b[i+1] for all 0 <= i < n-1, sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(b[i]-nums[i]) = r, and b[0] = nums[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums) returns a result r, there is exactly one integer array b of length n satisfying: b[i] >= nums[i] for all 0 <= i < n; b[i] < b[i+1] for all 0 <= i < n-1; and sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(b[i]-nums[i]) = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000.
